gp.heading: Gross Profit
gp.text:
Gross profit decreased $41.0 million, or 3.2%, to $1,222.0 million in 2024, compared to $1,263.0 million in 2023, primarily driven by lower net sales. As a percentage of net sales, our gross profit rate increased slightly to 44.9% in 2024, compared to 44.8% in 2023, primarily due to a higher gross margin rate at our Brand Portfolio segment. The gross margin at Brand Portfolio benefitted from higher merchandise margins and a higher mix of retail sales, including e-commerce sales from our owned brands and sales from our branded retail stores, both of which have higher gross margins than our wholesale sales. These increases were partially offset by a decrease in the gross margin rate at our Famous Footwear segment driven by higher levels of promotional activity and clearance sales.

We classify warehousing, distribution, sourcing and other inventory procurement costs in selling and administrative expenses. Accordingly, our gross profit and selling and administrative expenses, as a percentage of net sales, may not be comparable to other companies.

tax.text: Our consolidated effective tax rate was 21.5% in 2024, compared to 5.2% in 2023. Our lower tax rate for 2023 primarily reflected the release of $26.7 million of valuation allowances recorded for certain deferred tax assets. As a result of the significant loss before income taxes in 2020 driven by the impairment of goodwill and intangible assets during the pandemic, we entered into a three-year cumulative loss position for federal, state and certain international jurisdictions. At that time, we increased our valuation allowances on deferred tax assets to $50.0 million, reflecting the uncertainty regarding the utilization of our deferred tax assets in those jurisdictions. Due to stronger earnings in 2022 and 2023, the Company was no longer in a cumulative three-year loss position. Accordingly, the Company released valuation allowances on certain deferred tax assets totaling $26.7 million ($0.75 per diluted share) in 2023.

intro.text: Caleres, Inc. (the "Company"), originally founded as Brown Shoe Company in 1878 and incorporated in 1913, is a global footwear company that operates retail shoe stores and e-commerce websites, and designs, develops, sources, manufactures and distributes footwear for people of all ages. Our mission is to inspire people to feel great...feet first. We meet consumers where they want to shop, whether in-store or online. The Famous Footwear segment is comprised of our Famous Footwear retail stores, famousfootwear.com and famousfootwear.ca.

gp.text:
Gross profit decreased $41.0 million, or 3.2%, to $1,222.0 million in 2024, compared to $1,263.0 million in 2023, primarily driven by lower net sales. As a percentage of net sales, our gross profit rate increased slightly to 44.9% in 2024, compared to 44.8% in 2023, primarily due to a higher gross margin rate at our Brand Portfolio segment. The gross margin at Brand Portfolio benefitted from higher merchandise margins and a higher mix of retail sales, including e-commerce sales from our owned brands and sales from our branded retail stores, both of which have higher gross margins than our wholesale sales. These increases were partially offset by a decrease in the gross margin rate at our Famous Footwear segment driven by higher levels of promotional activity and clearance sales.

lines.name: Cash and cash equivalents
lines.why: Cash can repay debt or be paid out: a financial asset. Cash needed to run the business is operating; move it if you know how much.

lines.name: Receivables
lines.why: Owed by customers for sales: operating.

lines.name: Inventory
lines.why: Goods held for sale: operating.

lines.name: Prepaid and other current assets
lines.why: Prepayments and other operating items: operating.

lines.name: Property, plant and equipment
lines.why: Assets used to produce and sell: operating.

lines.name: Operating lease right-of-use assets
lines.why: Leased stores, offices and equipment used in the business: operating.

lines.name: Goodwill
lines.why: Paid for acquired businesses: operating.

lines.name: Intangible assets
lines.why: Acquired technology, brands and customer relationships: operating.

lines.name: Deferred tax assets
lines.why: Taxes on operating income paid ahead: operating.

lines.name: Other non-current assets
lines.why: Other long-term operating items: operating.

lines.name: Accounts payable
lines.why: Owed to suppliers for operations: operating.

lines.name: Accrued liabilities
lines.why: Services and other costs not yet paid: operating.

lines.name: Accrued compensation
lines.why: Wages, bonuses and benefits earned but not yet paid: operating.

lines.name: Income taxes payable
lines.why: Taxes on operating income: operating.

lines.name: Long-term debt (incl. current portion)
lines.why: Bonds, notes and loans, current maturities included: financial.

lines.name: Operating lease liabilities
lines.why: Rent owed on leases used in the business: operating by default. Move it to financing to treat leases like debt (if the balance sheet has no lease line of its own, they sit inside other liabilities).

lines.name: Income taxes payable, non-current
lines.why: Taxes on operating income due after a year (often uncertain tax positions): operating.

lines.name: Deferred tax liabilities
lines.why: Taxes on operating income deferred: operating.

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities
lines.why: Other long-term operating obligations: operating.

lines.name: Other current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current assets minus the current lines above: current assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current assets (total assets − current assets) minus the non-current lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current liabilities minus the current lines above: current liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current liabilities (total liabilities − current liabilities) minus the non-current lines above: liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.
